title: Add snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms for pre-T2 MacBook and iMac speakers
author: j7j7
body:
## Summary
- Adds `snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms` for the Cirrus CS8409 Apple speaker path ([davidjo/snd_hda_macbookpro](https://github.com/davidjo/snd_hda_macbookpro)).
- Includes @shawnyeager's packaging from #155 (full tree, `wget`/`patch` deps, correct `PACKAGE_NAME` install path) and widens `pkgdesc` / comments for **2017–2019 iMacs** as well as 2016–2017 MacBook Pros.
- Pairs with the omarchy install hook PR that detects `MacBookPro13,x` / `14,x` and `iMac18,x` / `iMac19,x`.

Pins commit `6c324f6` (verified on MacBookPro14,3 / linux 7.1.8). Same Apple CS8409 path applies to iMacs such as iMac18,3 (subsystem `0x106b1000`).

`source: local` so an AUR sync does not replace it. Provides/conflicts with `snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms-git`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Package builds in omarchy-pkgs pipeline
- [ ] On a CS8409 Mac: `omarchy-pkg-add linux-headers snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms` → DKMS install succeeds → reboot → speakers work

Can close #155 in favor of this once reviewed.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+# Maintainer: Omarchy <https://omarchy.org>
+# Upstream: https://github.com/davidjo/snd_hda_macbookpro
+#
+# The AUR package (snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms-git) copies only a subset of
+# the tree and does not depend on wget, which PRE_BUILD needs to fetch
+# matching kernel sources. This package installs the whole driver and
+# pins the commit verified on MacBookPro14,3 / linux 7.1.8. The same
+# Apple CS8409 path covers 2017–2019 iMacs (e.g. iMac18,3 subsystem
+# 0x106b1000).
+
+_pkgbase=snd-hda-macbookpro
+# Must match PACKAGE_NAME in upstream dkms.conf. The AUR dest uses hyphens
+# (snd-hda-macbookpro-0.1); Arch's alpm hook then runs
+# `dkms install snd-hda-macbookpro/0.1`, which exits 7 because PACKAGE_NAME
+# is snd_hda_macbookpro. omarchy-pkg-add relies on that hook.
+_srcname=snd_hda_macbookpro
+pkgname=${_pkgbase}-dkms
+pkgver=0.1
+pkgrel=3
+pkgdesc="DKMS driver for Cirrus CS8409 HDA on 2016–2017 MacBook Pros and 2017–2019 iMacs"
+arch=('x86_64')
+url="https://github.com/davidjo/snd_hda_macbookpro"
+license=('GPL-2.0-only')
+depends=('dkms' 'wget' 'patch')
+makedepends=('git')
+optdepends=('linux-headers: build against the Arch kernel')
+provides=('snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms-git')
+conflicts=('snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms-git')
+# 6c324f6: dkms.conf for current kernels; 6.17+ install path.
+_commit=6c324f6c9262faa853fdd74d798c5686937a9d0f
+source=("git+https://github.com/davidjo/snd_hda_macbookpro.git#commit=${_commit}")
+sha256sums=('SKIP')
+
+package() {
+    local dest="${pkgdir}/usr/src/${_srcname}-${pkgver}"
+
+    install -dm755 "$dest"
+    cp -a snd_hda_macbookpro/. "$dest/"
+    rm -rf "$dest/.git" "$dest/build"
+
+    # PRE_BUILD runs install.cirrus.driver.sh; the AUR package left these 0644.
+    chmod 755 "$dest"/install.cirrus.driver.sh \
+              "$dest"/install.cirrus.driver.pre617.sh \
+              "$dest"/dkms.sh
+}

comments.body:
Heads-up on `PRE_BUILD` before this lands, because as written it ships a
~151 MB download to every affected user on **every kernel update**.

`package()` copies the whole tree and removes only `.git` and `build/`, so
upstream's `dkms.conf` ships verbatim — including:

```
PRE_BUILD="install.cirrus.driver.sh -k $kernelver --dkms"
```

That script is what `wget` is a dependency for:

```
wget -c https://cdn.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/v$major_version.x/linux-$kernel_version.tar.xz -P $build_dir
```

For linux-7.1.9 that's 158,435,316 bytes, of which it uses **2,490,543** — only
`sound/hda`. Because `AUTOINSTALL="yes"`, it re-runs on every kernel bump, per
machine. Offline, behind a proxy, on a metered link, or on a box with a local
pacman mirror but no general internet, the DKMS build fails inside the pacman
transaction and the user's speakers go silent again after a routine update.

### This is avoidable, and omarchy-pkgs is the ideal place to avoid it

Everything `PRE_BUILD` does is deterministic and kernel-source-only: fetch
`sound/hda`, swap in upstream's cut-down `makefiles/`, copy the `patch_cirrus/`
headers, apply `patch_cs8409.{c,h}.diff`. None of it needs to happen on the
user's machine.

Since omarchy-pkgs builds packages centrally, doing it in `prepare()` means the
tarball is fetched **once in your pipeline**, not once per user per kernel. Ship
the prepared tree and drop `PRE_BUILD`; `dkms.conf` then reduces to:

```
MAKE[0]="make KERNELRELEASE=${kernelver}"
AUTOINSTALL="yes"
```

DKMS rebuilds run `make` and nothing else, and `wget` leaves `depends`.

Rough shape — add the kernel tarball to `source=()` with `noextract`, then:

```bash
prepare() {
  cd "$srcdir/snd_hda_macbookpro"
  install -d build
  tar --strip-components=2 -xf "$srcdir/linux-${_ksrcver}.tar.xz" \
      -C build "linux-${_ksrcver}/sound/hda"
  # upstream's cut-down Makefiles + patch_cirrus headers, then:
  cd build/hda
  patch -b -p1 <"$srcdir/snd_hda_macbookpro/patch_cs8409.c.diff"
  patch -b -p1 <"$srcdir/snd_hda_macbookpro/patch_cs8409.h.diff"
}
```

A working version is at
**https://github.com/ari-ahm/snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms** (GPL-2.0-only, same
`_commit` 6c324f6 you pin). It vendors its sources, which suits a local build
but probably isn't what you want in-repo — the `prepare()` and `dkms.conf` are
the transferable parts. Take, adapt or ignore; no attribution needed.

Verified under `unshare -n` with no network interfaces: both the DKMS rebuild
and `makepkg` itself succeed with cdn.kernel.org unreachable.

There's a second benefit for a distro package: patching at build time means a
conflict against a newer kernel fails your pipeline, instead of silently
breaking users' audio on a kernel update months later. The two diffs currently
apply to 7.1.9 with offsets and some fuzz, so that will matter eventually.

### Two smaller things

- The header comment says the AUR package *"does not depend on wget"*. It does —
  `snd-hda-macbookpro-dkms-git` `0.1-3` lists `wget` in `depends`. The other
  reasons for a separate package still hold (partial tree, exec bits, the
  `PACKAGE_NAME` mismatch making `dkms install` exit 7), so only the premise is
  off.
- `optdepends=('linux-headers: ...')` makes headers optional, which reproduces
  the silent failure described in omarchy#8285: with no headers, Arch's DKMS
  hook globs `usr/lib/modules/*/build`, matches nothing, builds nothing and
  exits 0, leaving `dkms status` empty and no error anywhere. It works today
  only because the install hook adds `linux-headers` separately. A hard
  `depends` would make the package correct on its own.

### Coverage data point

Confirmed working on **MacBookPro14,1** (codec subsystem `0x106b3300`), Omarchy
4.0.2, linux 7.1.9-arch1-2, gcc 16.2.1 — no source changes beyond upstream's own
two diffs — alongside the 14,3 and iMac18,3 already verified. Upstream handles `0x106b3300` and `0x106b3600` in the
same branch, so 13,1/14,1/14,2 come together.
